entries.title: The Best New Non-Fiction Kindle Books for August 2026
entries.summary: Top non-fiction Kindle book releases for August 2026 feature high-profile sports psychology, investigative environmental history, and cultural analysis. The post The Best New Non-Fiction Kindle Books for August 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Notable non-fiction books published in August 2026 span cultural commentary, investigative history, and economics. Highlights include Jill Lepore’s The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State, Claire Stapleton’s Don’t Be Evil, and Annie Lowrey’s The Time Tax.

Sale

Don't Be Evil: Bad Bosses Fake Promises and My Escape from Big Tech – A Biting Memoir of Twelve...

Don't Be Evil by Claire StapletonDon't Be Evil by Claire StapletonDon't Be Evil: Bad Bosses, Fake Promises, and My Escape from Big Tech is a sharp, darkly funny memoir written by former Google employee and labor activist Claire Stapleton. Published by William Morrow, the book chronicles her twelve-year journey at Google—from an eager college graduate to a disillusioned rebel who ultimately co-organized the historic 2018 Google Walkout.

Sale

The People's Historian: The Outsized Life of Howard Zinn

The People's Historian: The Outsized Life of Howard Zinn is a definitive, deeply researched biography written by The Nation magazine’s sports editor and bestselling author Dave Zirin. Published by Penguin Random House, the book offers an intimate portrait of Howard Zinn—the radical historian whose landmark 1980 text A People's History of the United States completely reshaped how modern Americans understand their own country's past.

Sale

Exhumed: Unearthing the History of the American Vampire

Exhumed: Unearthing the History of the American Vampire is a macabre, deeply researched historical narrative written by bestselling author and award-winning Lore podcaster Aaron Mahnke. Published by Running Press, the book draws from a decade of historical excavation to explore the bizarre, tragic intersection of pseudoscience, genuine medicine, and folklore in 19th-century America.

Sale

Your Fellow Americans: Dispatches from Across the Country We Call Home

Your Fellow Americans: Dispatches from Across the Country We Call Home is a deeply human, immersive travel memoir written by independent journalist, filmmaker, and popular YouTuber Peter Santenello. Published by Simon & Schuster, the book transitions his signature unfiltered video storytelling style to the page, documenting his journey into the heart of overlooked and misunderstood subcultures.

Sale

Mothers of Invention: A History of Creativity from the Greek Muses

Mothers of Invention: A History of Creativity from the Greek Muses is an innovative, sweeping historical narrative written by astrophysicist, folklorist, and science communicator Dr. Moiya McTier. Published by Grand Central Publishing, the book explores the evolution of human innovation through a witty, mythological lens, framing the history of science and art as a collaborative journey.

Sale

The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State

The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State is a passionate, alarming historical narrative and political critique written by Pulitzer Prize-winning Harvard historian and New Yorker staff writer Jill Lepore. Published by Liveright, the book investigates how data-driven automation has steadily replaced constitutional democracy, sounding an urgent wake-up call regarding the rise of algorithmic governance.

Sale

The Time Tax: How the Government Wastes Our Time—and How to Fix It

The Time Tax: How the Government Wastes Our Time—and How to Fix It is an enraging, deeply analytical investigation into modern bureaucracy written by renowned journalist and The Atlantic staff writer Annie Lowrey. Published by Ecco (an imprint of HarperCollins), the book gives a definitive name to the invisible bill every citizen is forced to pay: the endless paperwork, systemic friction, and mental exhaustion required to access basic rights and public benefits.

Sale

Biological War: A Scenario

Biological War: A Scenario is a terrifying, meticulously reported non-fiction thriller written by Pulitzer Prize finalist and investigative journalist Annie Jacobsen. Published by Dutton, the book follows the gripping, minute-by-minute narrative structure of her previous massive international bestseller, Nuclear War: A Scenario, tracking the rapid collapse of human society following the deployment of a biological weapon.

Sale

The American School of Spies: The Archaeologists Who Fought the Nazis and Saved the Treasures of...

The American School of Spies: The Archaeologists Who Fought the Nazis and Saved the Treasures of Ancient Greece is a narrative non-fiction history book written by New York Times bestselling author Stephan Talty.

Sale

The Cruelest Game: Chasing Greatness in Professional Tennis

The Cruelest Game: Chasing Greatness in Professional Tennis is an upcoming sports and psychology book by veteran journalist Matthew Futterman. The book is a revelatory exposé on the immense mental and physical toll of professional tennis. It features unprecedented, behind-the-scenes access to private practice courts, locker room tunnels, and training academies.

Sale

Tempted: My Story

Tempted My Story is an upcoming celebrity memoir co-authored by Canadian media personality Rick Campanelli and veteran broadcast writer John Meyer. The book details Campanelli's highly public television career contrasted against his hidden personal struggles. The memoir tracks his rapid rise from an unknown kid in Hamilton, Ontario, to a national superstar known affectionately as Rick the Temp after winning a nationwide contest to become a VJ on Canada's iconic MuchMusic station.

entries.title: The Best New Kindle Books for August 2026
entries.summary: Anticipated and trending top book releases for August 2026 include The Unknown by Riley Sager, Big Little Truths by Liane Moriarty, and Sunrise by Téa Obreht The post The Best New Kindle Books for August 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
August 2026 brings an exciting lineup of highly anticipated fiction, thrillers, and fantasy. Major releases include Chris Bohjalian’s legal thriller The Amateur, the chilling mystery The Truth About Ruby Cooper, and Karin Slaughter’s thriller The Secrets We Hide.

Sale

The Amateur: A Novel

The Amateur is a suspenseful 2026 novel by Chris Bohjalian, author of The Flight Attendant. Set in 1978, it follows Mira Winston, an 18-year-old golf prodigy whose stray practice shot fatally hits a caddy, triggering an investigation that exposes dark local secrets, class divides, and an illicit affair.

The Truth About Ruby Cooper: A Novel

The Truth About Ruby Cooper is a 2026 dark psychological thriller and domestic suspense novel written by internationally bestselling Irish author Liz Nugent.

Sale

The Secrets We Hide: A North Falls Thriller – The Next North Falls Thriller From Karin Slaughter...

The novel serves as Book 2 in the North Falls series, acting as the direct follow-up to her 2025 bestseller, We Are All Guilty Here. It features her signature gritty, emotionally heavy style while focusing on an inward-looking, rural Georgia community.

The Whitechapel Full Moon Society: A Novel

The Whitechapel Full Moon Society is an upcoming 2026 historical fantasy, mystery, and gothic thriller novel written by Southern Californian author Elizabeth DeLozier.The story takes place in 1888 Victorian London, right during the height of Jack the Ripper's reign of terror in the East End.

Sale

You'll Be Sorry

You'll Be Sorry is an upcoming 2026 small-town standalone psychological thriller written by #1 New York Times bestselling suspense author Lisa Gardner. While Gardner is highly celebrated for her ongoing criminal procedural universes—such as the Frankie Elkin, D.D. Warren, and FBI Profilers series—she explicitly noted that this specific story idea compelled her to write a completely standalone mystery.

Sale

The Seekers of Deer Creek: A Story of Two Sisters, a Lost Painting, and Their Search for the Truth

The Seekers of Deer Creek is an upcoming 2026 contemporary family saga, mystery, and literary fiction novel written by national bestselling author Thao Tha.It serves as Thai's highly anticipated sophomore novel following her decorated 2023 debut, Banyan Moon, which was a TODAY Show Read with Jenna Book Club pick and longlisted for the Center for Fiction's First Novel Prize.

Sale

The Unknown: A Novel

The Unknown is an upcoming 2026 gothic-tinted locked-room thriller and mystery novel written by New York Times bestselling author Riley Sager. The book serves as Sager’s tenth novel, marking a celebration of his 10-year milestone in the thriller genre since his breakout debut Final Girls.

Sale

Meet Me in Paris: A Novel

Meet Me in Paris is an upcoming 2026 contemporary romance, historical drama, and women's fiction novel by New York Times bestselling author Kristin Harmel. While Harmel is highly celebrated for her deep, immersive World War II historical fiction blockbusters—like The Book of Lost Names and The Winemaker's Wife—this project marks a major creative departure. Harmel explicitly stated that the book serves as a contemporary craft challenge inspired by her deep love for ensemble romantic-comedy-dramas. The overall structural style is heavily pitched as Love Actually meets The Notebook.

Sale

Big Little Truths: A Novel (Big Little series)

Big Little Truths is an upcoming 2026 contemporary family drama and domestic mystery novel written by #1 New York Times bestselling Australian author Liane Moriarty. It serves as the highly anticipated direct book sequel to her 2014 runaway phenomenon Big Little Lies, which inspired the award-winning, star-studded HBO television series.

Lost and Found: A Spunes Novel

Lost and Found is an upcoming 2026 small-town contemporary romance and emotional drama written by USA Today bestselling author Tarah DeWitt. It serves as Book 3 in the Spunes, OR series, following her popular previous hits Left of Forever and Savor It. Early reviews from NetGalley highlight it as a highly emotional slow-burn romance that acts as the perfect, bittersweet send-off for the series.

entries.title: The Best Travel Ebooks for Smarter, Lighter, More Inspired Trips
entries.summary: Travel ebooks have become the modern traveller’s best companion: lighter than a… The post The Best Travel Ebooks for Smarter, Lighter, More Inspired Trips first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Travel ebooks have become the modern traveller’s best companion: lighter than a guidebook, searchable in seconds, and easy to update or carry across multiple devices. For anyone planning a city break, long-haul adventure, sabbatical, road trip or cultural deep dive, the best travel ebooks fall into two broad camps: practical guides that help you plan, budget and navigate, and narrative travel writing that helps you understand a place before you arrive. The strongest choices combine both: they save you time while also making the journey feel richer.

A great starting point is the major guidebook series. Lonely Planet, Rough Guides, DK Eyewitness and Fodor’s remain dependable because they are built around traveller needs: neighbourhood breakdowns, suggested itineraries, maps, food tips, transport guidance and cultural context. Whop’s overview of travel ebooks highlights the core advantage of digital guides: they are searchable, weightless and often easier to update than print books, making them especially useful while moving between cities or countries. Rough Guides’ listings also show how many modern travel books now bundle print and ebook access, giving readers the convenience of both formats.

For first-time visitors to a destination, Lonely Planet’s pocket and regional ebooks are often among the most useful. Their strength is clarity: they quickly tell you what matters, what can be skipped and how to structure a short stay. Pocket guides are especially handy for weekend breaks because they prioritise compact itineraries over encyclopaedic detail. Lonely Planet’s Pocket Las Vegas listing, for example, promotes “perfect day” itineraries, walking tours and offline digital access, which is exactly the kind of practical functionality that makes ebooks valuable on the ground.

Rough Guides are ideal for travellers who want more texture. They tend to balance practical information with cultural history, giving readers enough context to feel oriented rather than simply directed. The Pocket Rough Guide Las Vegas edition, for instance, includes must-see attractions, hidden gems, itineraries, dining and shopping recommendations, day-trip inspiration and updates for returning visitors. Its ebook version is also available through library platforms such as Hoopla, showing how travel ebooks can be accessed beyond standard retail stores.

For visual planners, DK Eyewitness ebooks are hard to beat. Their appeal lies in photography, diagrams and neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood layouts. They are particularly good for museum-heavy cities, historic destinations and family trips where visual orientation matters. If you like to understand how a city fits together before you arrive, DK’s style can make planning feel less abstract and more intuitive. Unlike minimalist pocket guides, these ebooks are often best read before departure, then dipped into during the trip.

Budget-conscious travellers should look beyond destination guides and consider ebooks focused on travel strategy. Matt Kepnes, known as Nomadic Matt, is frequently listed among ebook-style travel resources, with titles on low-cost travel, travel hacking and working abroad. Travel Addicts’ ebook list includes budget and lifestyle titles such as How to Travel the World on $50 a Day, The Ultimate Guide to Travel Hacking and Teaching English Overseas, reflecting the strong demand for practical ebooks that help people travel longer for less. These are less about sightseeing and more about systems: flights, accommodation, rewards, budgeting and mindset.

Narrative travel ebooks offer something different: inspiration. The best ones do not tell you where to eat dinner; they change how you see movement, landscape and culture. Bill Bryson’s A Walk in the Woods, Cheryl Strayed’s Wild and Bryson’s Notes from a Small Island are regularly ranked among classic travel reads, with Shortform’s travel book list placing them near the top of its all-time rankings. These are ideal for armchair travel, long flights or pre-trip mood-setting, especially when you want personality and reflection rather than instructions.

Food and culture-focused travel ebooks also deserve attention. They are perfect for travellers who build trips around markets, restaurants, wine regions or local traditions. Recent travel-book roundups include food-led and place-led titles such as Caroline Eden’s Green Mountains, which blends travel writing with cuisine and regional history across Armenia, Georgia and the Black Sea. These ebooks are not always traditional “guides”, but they can make a trip more meaningful by helping readers understand what they are eating, why it matters and how food connects to identity.

Las Vegas deserves its own mention because it is one of the destinations where a good travel ebook can genuinely save money and stress. The city changes quickly, prices fluctuate around major events and the best experience is rarely just “walk the Strip and gamble”. A strong Vegas ebook should cover resort fees, transport, show booking, free attractions, Downtown Las Vegas, off-Strip dining and day trips such as Red Rock Canyon, Hoover Dam, Valley of Fire, Zion or the Grand Canyon. Rough Guides’ Vegas ebook highlights attractions including the Forum Shops, the Venetian, Omega Mart, Red Rock Canyon, Bellagio, the Neon Museum, Hoover Dam and Valley of Fire, making it useful for travellers who want more than casinos or online slots. Lonely Planet’s Pocket Las Vegas also focuses on quick-hit itineraries and unexpected experiences, including Death Valley road trips and major casino-resort landmarks.

Ultimately, the “best” travel ebook depends on the type of trip. Choose Lonely Planet for efficient planning, Rough Guides for depth, DK for visual orientation, Fodor’s for polished mainstream recommendations, budget ebooks for long-term travel tactics and narrative travel writing for inspiration. The smartest approach is to combine one practical guide with one reflective read: one helps you move through a destination confidently; the other helps you notice it properly.

Markus lives in San Francisco, California and is the video game and audio expert on Good e-Reader! He has a huge interest in new e-readers and tablets, and gaming.

entries.title: Harry Potter e-books and audiobooks are now on Kobo Plus
entries.summary: The entire Harry Potter book series is available for free on Kobo Plus. You can access both the digital novels and the official audiobooks directly through your subscription tiers. The post Harry Potter e-books and audiobooks are now on Kobo Plus first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
This month, the complete Harry Potter series is available on Kobo Plus, making it available to subscribers to enjoy as part of their monthly membership. Whether readers are revisiting Hogwarts years later or discovering the series for the very first time, Kobo Plus offers an easy way to dive into one of the world’s most beloved literary franchises alongside access to a growing catalogue of eBooks and audiobooks.

“The impact of the Harry Potter series is unprecedented. While the Harry Potter titles have always been popular on Kobo, we are so excited to bring them and other stories from the Wizarding World to our Kobo Plus subscribers. After over a decade as pioneers in the digital reading space, we’ve learned that nothing excites a booklover as much as saying ‘read as much as you want,’ which is exactly what our Kobo Plus service offers,” said Bart Robers, Director, Audiobooks and Global Subscriptions, Rakuten Kobo.

  • Read the complete Harry Potter eBook Seriesincluding Philosopher’s Stone and Deathly Hallows for $9.99/month.
  • Stream the full catalog of Harry Potter Audiobooksnarrated by Stephen Fry or Jim Dale for $9.99/month.
  • Combine both catalogs for a bundled price of $12.99/month to switch seamlessly between reading and listening

entries.title: New Onyx Boox Picco wants to compete against XTEINK
entries.summary: The BOOX Picco is a pocket-sized eReader that Onyx Boox teased as the first device in its new Tile product line. The post New Onyx Boox Picco wants to compete against XTEINK first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
XTEINK is a Chinese technology brand known for creating ultra-thin, distraction-free pocket E-Ink e-readers designed to snap magnetically to the back of a smartphone like a MagSafe accessory. These viral, “purse-sized” devices are engineered for digital minimalism, featuring ultra-light builds, zero notifications, and weeks of battery life. Onyx Boox has realized these guys are controlling the small-sized e-reader market and is working on their own product called the BOOX Picco.

The BOOX Picco 3.97inch e-reader and is currently being teased by Onyx Boox. It will feature a black-and-white e-paper display with E INK technology. Users will be able to read during the day or night via the front-lit display, and upgraded storage will be available via an SD card. There appear to be buttons on the promotional image for page turns, it is also heavily rumoured this device is apart of a new Tile product line.

If Onyx wants to compete against XTEINK, they will have to keep the price down to around $99 to $129 maximum. This will likely result in some sacrifices, such as not using a touchscreen and having very limited tech specs and a custom UI that is geared towards reading and not much else. It is likely it will have a tiled design, which are a series of UI elements that are locked into positioned, so think the Neoreader app for reading, a music player, podcast player and that is about it. For users who want a better experience, such as installing apps, there is always the Palma 2 that retails for 269.99.

entries.title: Kindle Read Sample button is now working again
entries.summary: There was a major bug that prevented people from reading Kindle Book Samples, three days later the issue has been fixed by Amazon. The post Kindle Read Sample button is now working again first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Three days after being completely broken, the Read Sample button on Kindle Books is now working again. Customers can now use the Amazon website on an internet browser, mobile website, or the Kindle reading app for Android and iOS.

Initially, when the Read Sample button was broken, there was no way to read the first few chapters for free to see if buying the book was a worthwhile investment. Now that the sample button is fixed, customers can once again use it on all of their devices and on the Amazon website.

The “Read Sample” (or “Look Inside”) button allows you to preview the first chapter of a book before purchasing. On the Amazon website, it is typically located below the book’s cover image. If you are using a mobile device, you will usually see a “Look Inside the Book” sticker instead.

entries.title: Modos Flow E INK Monitor is now available for pre-order
entries.summary: Modos Flow is the result: a responsive, paper-like, 13.3-inch monitor built for everyday reading, writing, and focused work. This product uses an E Ink® display. It connects over USB Type-C’s DisplayPort Alt Mode and supports touch as part of everyday use. The color model also includes a built-in frontlight and stylus support. The post Modos Flow E INK Monitor is now available for pre-order first
entries.content:
The Modos Flow is an open-hardware, 13.3-inch E Ink monitor designed for comfortable, paper-like desktop use with a highly responsive 60 Hz refresh rate. Developed by Modos Tech and funded via a Crowd Supply campaign, the monitor bridges the gap between traditional static e-readers and the low latency needed for daily productivity tasks like reading, writing, and coding. There are two variants: the color e-paper version, which costs $799, and the black and white model for $699.

The Flow features a 13.3-inch E INK Carta 1300 e-paper display with a 3200 x 2400 resolution and 300 PPI and 150 PPI for the Kaleido 3 color version. The monitor includes built-in touch support, an adjustable dual-tone frontlight, and an integrated cover that folds out into a portable kickstand. The display relies on an AMD Zynq 7000 SoC controller with fully open-source firmware and public hardware schematics on GitHub. This allows custom developer modifications in Rust, Python, and C via the Modos Flow API.

It uses open-source firmware and hardware, allowing for customization and repairability. With some fancy software trickery, Modos offers four different viewing modes: browsing, typing, watching, and reading. They will change the refresh rate based on the type of content you want. The highest resolution is for reading, and for watching videos, it will have a fast mode to handle 60 Hz refresh rates.

The monitor can connect to your computer with USB Type-C or DisplayPort and is compatible with Linux, macOS, and Windows.

entries.title: The Light Phone Flip coming out in 2027
entries.summary: The Light Flip is a minimalist, distraction-free 5G flip phone. It is designed to reduce digital clutter by completely omitting social media, web browsers, and email. The post The Light Phone Flip coming out in 2027 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Light Flip is a minimalist, distraction-free 5G clamshell phone designed by Light. It strips away social media, web browsers, and infinite scrolling to help users reduce screen time. Unlike their previous phones, which have an E INK screen, this one only has an OLED.

The Light Flip features a 2.8-inch OLED screen with a resolution of 480×640 and has a matte screen protector installed at the factory to help eliminate the glare from the sun and other overhead lighting. Under the hood is a MediaTek MT8873 processor, 6GB of RAM, and 128GB of internal storage. Two microphones with noise cancellation are good for calls, and it has two stereo speakers for speakerphone. 5G and 4G LTE connectivity, the Light Flip can download podcasts online and play music that you upload to your phone, which you can listen to via either a 3.5 mm headphone jack or Bluetooth headphones. It charges via USB-C, works with both eSIM and physical Nano SIM cards, and includes a 12-megapixel camera on the back. It is powered by a 1800 mAh battery, which is fully removable with common tools and is rated IP54.

There is no touchscreen on the phone; instead, it has a user-friendly 12-button keypad that will feel nostalgic for anyone who used T9 for texting or remembers dialing on a landline. It includes three function buttons, with the middle one integrated into a four-way directional pad to easily navigate the phone’s cursor. Additionally, there’s a home button conveniently placed on the side, along with volume control switches nearby.

Why a flip phone? Light’s founder Joe Hollier and Kaiwei Tang told TechCrunch that they’ve gotten a lot of requests for the form factor, particularly from younger users who want a phone that’s even less smartphone-like than the Light Phone III. They’ve also seen lots of people in “distraction-free” communities move to old-school flip phones — but most new flip phones in production are not terribly capable.

Light offers the Flip in a range of colors: black, red, yellow, pink, navy blue, and light gray, and is available as a pre-order on their website for $299.99. It is not planned to ship until April of 2027, so it won’t be out anytime soon.

However, there are a few drawbacks that will prevent me from buying it. It has no touchscreen, selfie camera, or NFC. The body is made of plastic and doesn’t have an E-ink display. It only has a music and podcast app, but the company is promising an SDK for developers to work on third-party apps.

entries.title: Audible announces New Full-Cast Adaptation of Dracula
entries.summary: Rather than a traditional audiobook, Dracula has been developed as a full-cast audio drama featuring Hollywood talent, an original score, and immersive sound design. The post Audible announces New Full-Cast Adaptation of Dracula first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible has announced its forthcoming adaptation of Dracula – an Audible Original that reimagines Bram Stoker’s chilling psychological thriller as an immersive, full-cast audio experience. Launching globally on October 1, 2026, Dracula will be released in English, Castilian Spanish, French, German, Italian, Latin American Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese, with each production featuring an all-star local cast.

When her fiancé vanishes in Transylvania, Mina Murray pieces together fragments of letters, diary entries and chilling testimony to hunt the predator stalking those she loves, only to discover he’s already hunting her. When Mina’s closest friend Lucy succumbs to his thrall, the enigmatic Professor Van Helsing is summoned to wage war on this unfathomable threat. But it is Mina, with her intellect, her resolve, her gift for drawing unseen lines between clues, who may hold the key to stopping this ancient predator—if he hasn’t already found his way inside her mind.

The English-language production stars Jonathan Bailey (Wicked) as Dracula, Ella Purnell (Fallout) as Mina, Aimee Lou Wood (The White Lotus) as Lucy, Louis Partridge (Enola Holmes) as Jonathan, David Jonsson (Industry) as Dr Seward, Lesley Manville (Phantom Thread) as Mrs. Westenra and Maggie Gyllenhaal (The Dark Knight) as Professor Van Helsing.

Aurelie de Troyer, Head of Audible Content, International, said: “This is what Audible does best,crafting immersive audio experiences that transport listeners into the heart of the story. When Dracula whispers in your ear, when you hear his footsteps in the dark but see no reflection, that’s when you understand why we’re the home for this story. Our production elevates the psychological thriller at Dracula’s core, with the battle between Mina and Dracula as the heart of it all.”

She continued, “We’ve assembled world-class casts across seven languages, from Jonathan Bailey and Ella Purnell to Omar Sy, Riccardo Scamarcio and Matthias Schweighöfer, exceptional international talent delivering a truly global Dracula. With director Mary Lambert at the helm and a haunting score by Ilan Eshkeri, we’re bringing this ambitious production to life just in time for Halloween.”

entries.title: The XTEINK X4 Pro e-reader is now available
entries.summary: The XTEINK X4 Pro is an ultra-compact, pocket-sized e-reader priced at $99 USD. Designed to combat doomscrolling by offering a distraction-free reading experience, it features a magnetic backplate that allows it to attach directly to the back of MagSafe- or Qi2-compatible smartphones. The post The XTEINK X4 Pro e-reader is now available first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The XTEINK X4 Pro e-reader is now available and ready to order from the company’s website for around $99. It is designed as a premium alternative to the original minimalist XTEINK X4; it introduces highly requested modern features while maintaining its ultra-portable, distraction-free identity. The big selling points are the new touchscreen and front-lit display, two features that are sure to impress; however, it no longer has a USB-C port.

The X4 Pro features a 4.3-inch E-Ink touchscreen with a resolution of 220 PPI. The lighting system is the most anticipated upgrade. It allows you to read comfortably in the dark or in low-light environments without needing a separate clip-on reading lamp. Despite adding layers for the light and touch sensors, the Pro model measures an incredibly slim 5.98mm, making it slightly thinner than the original X4’s 6.4mm. It retains its physical page-turn buttons alongside the new touchscreen, giving you tactile control when flipping pages.

There will be 16 GB of fixed internal memory for reading e-books, but it is an SD card and it is capable of storing up to 256GB. There is a paltry 8MB RAM and Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz) and Bluetooth. It is powered by a 1100mAh battery, which should be enough for a month of reading. Unlike the standard USB-C on the first-generation X4, the X4 Pro utilizes a magnetic bespoke/pogo-pin charging cable (using a USB-C adapter). The native software supports ebooks in TXT, EPUB, MOBI, and PDF formats, along with JPG and PNG image formats.

This device retails for $99 from the XTEINK website.
